title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: we continue to see model-specific performance regressions / suboptimal throughput for some open models (notably Llama-family parameterizations, Mistral's nonstandard block shapes, and Qwen's rotary/dilation quirks) when running under the unified serving runtime and default quantization paths. Additionally, grouped quantization (GQA) and mixed-quant (MQA) defaults are not tuned per-model, which causes either quality regressions or missed perf opportunities for production workloads. This PR implements a set of targeted runtime optimizations and per-model tuning heuristics: kernel selection fallbacks, scheduler hints for continuous batching, KV cache prefretch/pinning heuristics, and GQA/MQA parameter defaults tuned for each model family. The goal is to improve tail latency, steady-state throughput, and unit token cost with minimal quality impact and no API changes. What changed (summary): - Kernel selection: add model-aware kernel selector that prioritizes fused attention/FFN kernels for Llama variants with head-dim divisibility; fall back to generic kernels for edge shapes. This reduces kernel launch overhead for common Llama widths and avoids pathological cases that triggered small-kernel thrash. - Qwen rotary handling: introduce a rotary-dilation-aware attention kernel path that properly handles Qwen's non-power-of-two rotary frequency packing. Fixes misaligned vector loads and reduces register spilling for >8k contexts. - Mistral block shapes: add a specialized matmul tiling path for Mistral 7B/8B block patterns (2-stage block layout). Improves GEMM throughput on Ampere+ hardware by reducing shared-memory bank conflicts. - Scheduler / continuous batching: add a short-seq-priority policy in continuous batching to group short requests together while allowing long requests to spill to dedicated lanes; improve latency SLO adherence under mixed workloads. Includes a configurable latency-priority factor per model. - KV cache heuristics: implement prefix pinning (pin last N cached KV pages for high-reuse prefixes), proactive KV prefetch for repeated prefixes and autoregressive hot-prefix detection (TTL-based). Reduces cold-KV misses for common chat scenarios. - GQA/MQA tuning: introduce per-model default groupsize and symmetric-scaling parameters (GQA groupsize, MQA block-size) with conservative defaults for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families. Add a runtime dry-run eval that logs embedding/LLM output divergence for a small prompt set to detect quality regressions when changing quant params. - Tests & benchmarks: microbench harness updates + new perf suite runs for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Qwen-7B to capture latency/throughput before/after. Behavioral notes / fallbacks: all optimizations are opt-out by model config flags and fall back to the legacy execution path if kernel dispatch fails, or if the runtime detects numerical instability beyond a conservative threshold. The per-model tuning table is shipped as part of model-registry metadata and can be overridden via runtime config. Performance results (selected): - Llama-2-13B (seq=512, batch=8): median latency -18%, p99 -14%, throughput +22% - Mistral-7B (seq=1024, batch=16): median latency -12%, throughput +15% - Qwen-7B (seq=4096, batch=4, long-prefix scenarios): p99 latency -27%, KV miss rate reduced ~40% - Token-cost estimate (internal accounting): net per-token GPU time reduced by ~11% on mixed workloads. Checklist: - [x] Kernel selector + kernels implemented - [x] Scheduler policy and continuous-batching integration - [x] KV pinning/prefetched implementation + unit tests - [x] GQA/MQA per-model defaults + dry-run quality check - [x] Microbench harness & perf reports attached - [x] Docs: runtime tuning guide + model registry entries updated - [x] Feature gated and overridable Commits (high level): - Add model-aware kernel selector and dispatch tests - Implement rotary-dilation-aware attention kernel for Qwen - Add Mistral block-tiling matmul path - Continuous batching: short-seq-priority policy and config knobs - KV cache: pinning, prefetch, and hot-prefix detector - GQA/MQA: per-model defaults and dry-run eval logging - Perf harness updates and benchmark results - Docs and model-registry metadata updates Files changed (high level): - runtime/kernel/selectors.cc | +420 -31 (new selector and heuristics) - runtime/kernels/attn_qwen.cu | +310 -12 (new specialized kernel) - runtime/kernels/matmul_mistral.cu | +265 -8 (tiling path) - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.cc | +190 -60 (policy integration) - runtime/kv_cache/kv_pin.cc | +140 -10 (pin/prefetch) - model-registry/model_tuning.yaml | +48 -2 (per-model defaults) - tests/perf/bench_model_families.py | +120 -5 (bench suite) - docs/runtime/tuning.md | +70 -3 Review conversation (highlights): - Sofia Chen (review): "Great work on isolating kernels per-model. A couple of questions: 1) numeric-stability thresholds and how we detect divergence for GQA dry-run; 2) can we gate the Qwen kernel on sm>=80?" - Arjun (reply): "Added conservative numeric divergence detector (L2 diff + token-level top-k overlap) and fallback path. Qwen kernel now checks compute capability at runtime, and we added a soft-fail to the generic kernel for older cards." - Maya Rodriguez (review): "Please add an integration test that exercises KV prefetch with chat-style reuse; also ensure metrics emitted for KV hit/miss are standardized." - Arjun: "Added integration test and prometheus metric renames (kv_cache_hits/kv_cache_misses)." - Ethan Li (approve): "Perf numbers are convincing and we have sensible fallbacks. Approving pending a short doc paragraph on how teams can override per-model defaults." - Arjun (reply): "Doc paragraph added to docs/runtime/tuning.md" CI status and checks: [unit tests: pass], [integration: pass], [perf-suite: pass (bench nodes)], [lint: pass], [docs build: pass]. One perf run initially showed a non-deterministic regression on old cuda-11 infra; added a guard that skips optimized kernels on unsupported toolchains and re-ran. Migration / rollout plan: - Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for models in the tuning table for 48 hours, watch p50/p95/p99 and quality dry-run logs. - If stable, increase to 50% then full rollout over 72 hours. - Dedicated/Dedicated private customers: config flag shipped in release notes; teams can opt-in via runtime config. Release notes: "Improved runtime performance for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen model families via model-aware kernels, scheduler tweaks, KV cache heuristics, and per-model GQA/MQA tuning. Expect lower latency and higher throughput for common production workloads. Feature is opt-out and gated by model registry flags." Follow-ups (planned): - Expand per-model tuning table to other families (e.g., Falcon, Baichuan) and consolidate auto-profiling steps into model onboarding. - Add automatic telemetry-driven tuning job (offline) to propose GQA/MQA parameter updates. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids aggressive quantization defaults; the dry-run divergence logs let us safely evaluate quality impact before flipping to more aggressive group sizes.
